findings.title: From concealment to self-disclosure
findings.claim: The brothers' later admission can be heard as bringing their own culpability into public speech after an earlier scene of concealed assessment, non-disclosure, and accusation.
findings.mechanism: In 12:77 Joseph keeps an assessment within himself, does not disclose it to the brothers, and names what they describe. In 12:91 the same group speaks publicly and names itself among the culpable. The earlier withholding and the later self-description contact through the brothers' speech and guilt term, shifting the focus from a sudden admission to a disclosure they now make themselves.
findings.reader_payoff: The brothers move from being the objects of an unspoken assessment to voicing an assessment of their own conduct.
findings.containment: The interior assessment in 12:77 belongs to Joseph; this does not claim that the brothers disclose the same thought or that Joseph had voiced a verdict against them. The connection may also remain dramatic irony rather than a deliberate lexical echo.

epistemic.reason: The context roots and word indices match the supplied 12:77 surface, and the focus speech and culpability carriers are present. The directional arc is an attributed HFT inference, with dramatic irony left open.

findings.title: Confession opens into non-reproach
findings.claim: After recognition and patience in 12:90, the brothers name God's preference and their own culpable wrong; Joseph's immediate no-reproach, forgiveness, and mercy answer that confession, while the host basmala's mercy-root echo and 12:93's transferred garment and summoned family extend the reply toward restoration.
findings.mechanism: Recognition in 12:90 and Joseph's statement that God does not waste the reward of the patient form the setting for the focus. The attributed HFT reading hears the brothers' confession as truth replacing defensive speech. In 12:92 Joseph answers with no reproach, forgiveness, and mercy, directly receiving the fault they named; the mercy root also echoes the host surah's opening basmala. In 12:93 the garment is carried to Jacob's face and the family is summoned, making the attributed kinship resonance concrete in a restorative sequence. The reply does not deny the act or keep it active as blame.
findings.reader_payoff: Accountability and restoration can coexist: the confession becomes a threshold into renewed relation rather than a terminal sentence of shame.
findings.containment: The HFT's truth-over-defense effect and kinship reading within the mercy root remain attributed; the basmala is a host-surah frame, not an explanation of why Joseph forgives. The later garment sequence does not show that confession earned pardon or that preference caused the garment's effect. Joseph's reply could be gracious without changing the focus utterance's force; forgiveness does not erase the admitted deed.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence directly supports the confession, no-reproach, covering, and mercy relation. Recognition and patience in 12:90, the host basmala's repeated mercy root, and the 12:93 restoration sequence are supplied surfaces; the HFT's changed-speech and kinship readings remain attributed.

findings.title: A trace carried toward restoration
findings.claim: The focus preference can also resonate as a remaining mark whose effects travel: the next scene sends Joseph's garment to Jacob's face, announces restored sight, and gathers the family.
findings.mechanism: The registered remaining-mark facet of the focus preference meets the concrete garment associated with Joseph in 12:93. The garment is cast onto the father's face and sight is announced restored; the family is then summoned. This sequence supplies a material carrier and direction for an exploratory reading in which preference leaves a transmissible effect that reaches perception and reunion.
findings.reader_payoff: The preference can be perceived as more than a named rank: the next action gives it a possible material trace and a path toward recognition and reunion.
findings.containment: The text does not state that the garment is literally the lexical trace of preference or that the garment's effect is caused by the preference. Physical sight and inner recognition remain parallel attributed readings.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and its core facet are registered, and every 12:93 root/index trace matches the supplied Arabic. The arrow from divine preference to an effect-bearing garment is the HFT reader's exploratory inference.

findings.title: Preference beside a path of favor
findings.claim: Fatiha 1:7 can add direction to the focus: Joseph's preference is heard beside a path explicitly associated with those God favors, so the clause can resonate as more than a comparison of rank.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb names Joseph as preferred over the brothers. Fatiha 1:7 names the straight path as the path of those whom God favored. This distinct-root contact meets the preference carrier with a path explicitly defined by bestowed favor, adding a directional frame to the local comparison.
findings.reader_payoff: The brothers' recognition can resonate as naming a preference within a trajectory of divine favor, not only a sibling ranking.
findings.containment: The different roots are not lexical equivalents; this does not identify Joseph with the Fatiha group or assign the brothers to its astray group. The pericope reading stands without this analogy.

epistemic.reason: The preference branch and the exact 1:7 path/favor surface are supplied; the shift from preference to a path-shaped register is an analogical resonance.
